title_pattern: First-person family-rule confession: 'My dad never allows anything with the number 6 in the house'. Formula = [My + family member] + [never allows / forbids] + [mundane thing defined by an oddly specific attribute] + [in the house]. The rule is absurd-but-concrete (a single digit), instantly raises 'why?', and implies a hidden family secret without saying horror. Hashtag tail (#mestery misspelt) + character name 'Chenjie' for series search. Per BRIEF rule 5 this is a translated repost of a Chinese animated drama (Chinese UI text, 保安 vest, 银行 SMS); study structure only.

thumbnail.why_it_works: One idea repeated everywhere (the number 6 is forbidden: crossed-out 6s), a readable title-as-thumbnail, a clear emotional face (fear + guilt), a looming authority figure, and a mysterious object (the box) that the viewer can't explain. Red/black screams horror in the feed. It promises a rule + a secret, which the video delivers in the first 20 s.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: My dad never allowed anything with the number six in the house. Phone numbers, addresses, prices, tags. If it had a six, he'd lose it completely.
hook.verbatim_0_12s: My dad never allowed anything with the number six in the house. Phone numbers, addresses, prices, tags. If it had a six, he'd lose it completely. So, I asked in a mental health group if this counted as OCD. But instead of answers, I got a weird warning. Delete that message now if you want to live. Never ask your dad why he's afraid of the number six.
hook.verbatim_12_24s: My aunt didn't take it seriously. For my dad's birthday, she sent six flowers and a check for 60,000. The night she gave them, my aunt was found dead in her own home. The number six was written all over her body, but the medical examiner couldn't figure out how she died.
hook.device: Title repeated verbatim as line 1 (thumbnail-to-video continuity), then a rapid list of concrete examples (phone numbers, addresses, prices, tags), then a stranger's threat that defines a FORBIDDEN QUESTION ('never ask your dad why'). Proof-of-stakes within 20 s: the aunt breaks the rule and dies with 6s written on her body. The forbidden question becomes the story's engine and the final payoff (the son asks it on purpose at 19:15). Visual cuts every 2 s in the first minute (8 different images in 20 s).

beats.summary: States the bizarre household rule (no 6s), lists absurd examples, then the instant escalation: asking about it online triggers a death warning from a stranger.
'Never ask your dad why he's afraid of six.' Aunt ignores it, sends 6 flowers and a 60,000 cheque, and is found dead with 6s written on her body. Death shown in the first 20 s.
Origin of the phobia (SIM card ending 6464), the rule spreading through the house, door 906 renamed 905+1, Dad's enemy-like stare.

Son posts in the group; 'Mystery Man' spams warnings, DMs him, recites private family details (names, dead mother), forces him to delete the post, gives THE rule: never ask the question or Dad and you die.
Aunt mocks it as a scam and vows to ask Dad herself (set-up of the rule-break by a side character).
Dad over-caring with soup, picks out carrot/corn slices that look like 6, missing wristwatch because its face had a 6. Small creepy details as re-hooks.
Aunt phones Dad and asks; Dad flees in terror to the bathroom; aunt's farewell voice message; Dad emerges: 'Your aunt is already dead.'
Mystery Man ('Master') reframes Dad as the villain: the 'Six-Star Death Box' made of meteorite iron; Dad's fake overtime and returning covered in dirt.
The box: six lights, five lit red, each needs a family member's life; voice recognition kills whoever asks the question. 'And I was next.'
Dad outside the door; Dad caresses the box with Mom's photo; finger-bite test shows no blood; Dad locks him in; Mystery Man says flee tonight with the box; bank alert shows Dad emptied his savings.
PART 2 begins. Balcony jump, grabs box, staircase loop that keeps returning him to the 6th floor and the guard Old Lee; jade pendant with 六 morphs into a car; Old Lee revealed as Dad's ally.
Escape in Mystery Man's red car to a suburban workshop; he hacks the box with a laptop; lights go out one by one while the son's head splits with pain.
Hidden chest with an old photo of the aunt defaced by red 6s, long before her death: the helper may be the villain. Son collapses.

Old Lee and Dad storm in, baton blow, lights come back on and pain stops; Dad/Old Lee claim the Mystery Man used the son to steal the box for his own dying son; a second faded photo; Dad knocks son out (cut to black).
Wakes half-conscious hearing Dad commit his fortune to a '6 in 10 chance'; Mystery Man tied up tries to ask the forbidden question and is clubbed; son holds the box hostage to force the truth.

Dad confesses: son died/was fatally hit saving a boy in a yellow raincoat; aunt murdered by a hired psychopath; Dad, an ex-scientist, keeps the son alive with cosmic matter (why he can't bleed); medicine in the box needs 6 lights x 6 days; the question is the self-destruct keyword.

Son deduces the medicine makes his genes match Dad's for an organ transplant, i.e. Dad will die for him; ignores Dad's begging and deliberately asks 'Why are you so afraid of the number six?' The box goes dark.
Old Lee reveals he arranged the accident and took the guard job to experiment on them; Dad threatens police; Old Lee offers a storage-unit stasis for 36 days.
Son runs out so Dad won't die for him; one-line VO 'ran till his death. The end of story.' No CTA.

pacing.note_wpm: ~280 wpm: TTS narration sped up (~1.4x natural). Dialogue-heavy (about 60% quoted dialogue between son, Dad, aunt, Mystery Man, Old Lee) read by one or two TTS voices.
pacing.note_shots: Frame-diff on 2 s samples found 264 visual changes (122 in Part 1, 142 in Part 2) => ~4.7 s between detectable changes; ffmpeg scene detect found 130 hard cuts. In the first 60 s a new picture appears every ~2 s; later the phone-call stretches hold one of two speaker frames for 2-6 s and change only the mouth/eyes and the caption. Real perceived pace is set by the caption changing every ~1.5-2.5 s.
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: ~30-60 s: a new rule, death, object, or twist roughly every 45 s (aunt death 0:18, door 905+1 0:40, private details 1:15, aunt rule-break 3:55, aunt dead 4:46, Death Box 6:10, five lights 7:15, no blood 8:35, savings emptied 9:36, stair loop 10:20, pendant morph 10:57, aunt photo 12:40, ambush 13:20, blackout 15:10, confession 16:40, the question asked 19:15, villain twist 20:00).
pacing.structure: Two-part compilation stitched into one 20-min upload: Part 1 (0:00-9:44) and Part 2 (9:44-20:41) with different caption styling and a 'Part 2' pill; tense shifts from past to present at ~15:40 (translation seam).
pacing.caption_style: Part 1: one-two line white sentence-case sans (~3% of frame height) centred in the black bar ABOVE the picture, dialogue in quotes. Part 2: white bold italic condensed uppercase comic font BELOW the picture, karaoke-ish emphasis (key phrase larger, others greyed); captions drop out entirely in several Part 2 stretches (14:02-14:58, 20:10-20:34).
pacing.music_sfx: Constant low music bed (auto-subs mark [music] about every 10-20 s); SFX implied by visual effects (phone buzz zap icon, smoke-puff fights, blackout).

techniques_worth_copying: Forbidden-question engine: one specific question that kills whoever asks it. Introduce it in the first 12 s, prove it in 20 s with a side character, and make the protagonist ask it on purpose at the climax.

Number-as-antagonist: a single digit (6) recurs everywhere (door 906 -> 905+1, SIM 6464, watch face, carrot slices, 6 lights, every 6 days, 36 days, pendant 六, '6 in 10 chance'). Cheap to animate and builds a pattern the viewer starts spotting themselves.
Absurd-but-concrete household rule in the title, repeated as the first spoken line.
Proof-of-stakes cold open: show the consequence (a body marked with the symbol) inside 20 s, then rewind to the origin.
Unseen-messenger device: a stranger who knows private family details (names, dead mother) in DMs/voice calls; plays as both mentor and suspect.
Small uncanny domestic details as re-hooks between plot beats (soup with 6-shaped slices removed, missing watch, Dad coming home covered in dirt, finger that won't bleed).
Countdown object with visible state: six lights, five lit. Each light = a life. Lights dimming/relighting gives a visual tension meter for the whole second act.
Serial role reversals: Dad villain -> Mystery Man villain -> Dad as self-sacrificing hero -> guard as true villain. Every reversal recontextualises earlier details.
Ambiguous hero-wants-to-be-dead ending (organ transplant sacrifice refused) with an abrupt one-line close.
Two-tier caption system: a dialogue line in quotes vs narration, so a single TTS voice can carry multiple characters.
code_only_remake_needs: Layout: 1080x1920 canvas, black background, 1080x~1000 picture band at y~25-55%, caption slot above (part-1 style) or below (part-2 style), small handle watermark lower third. Optional 'Part N' pill.

Character rig (SVG): 4-5 flat chibi-ish characters with big heads; swappable eye sets (normal, narrowed, huge white bug-eyes for shock, spiral/pupil-less for terror), mouth visemes for talk flaps, sweat drop, red anger-vein symbol; 2-3 poses each (standing, on phone, holding object, lying sideways collapsed).

Backgrounds as flat vector rooms: beige doorway with handle, dark blue room with lamp arcs (mentor's lair), navy sofa + window, wooden kitchen, stairwell landing with floor number, car interior, workshop shelves. 6-8 backgrounds cover the whole story.

Prop inserts: door plates with editable numbers, SIM card, wristwatch face, phone chat UI (group chat bubbles, voice-message bubble, bank SMS), glowing cube with N lights whose state is driven by data, framed photo with red scrawl overlay, pendant that morphs (SVG path morph).

Shot grammar: hard cuts every 2-4 s, shot-reverse-shot for phone calls (two framings alternated by speaker turn from the storyboard), slow 3-5% push-ins on reveals, camera shake on shocks, smoke-puff cloud sprite for fights, cut-to-black for blackout.
Captions: TTS word timings -> 1-2 line chunks of 6-10 words; dialogue in quotes; a highlight style for key nouns/numbers (red for the motif number).
Audio: fast TTS (~250-280 wpm) with 2 voices (narrator/son and others), low drone music bed, SFX for phone buzz, light-on ding, impact thud.
Storyboard data: per beat a list of {speaker, line, background, characters+expressions, prop insert, light_state}. The box light_state as a visible progress meter is the single most reusable element.
notes: Long-form 20:41 vertical upload; outlier ~2.9x the channel median. Part 2 visibly lower production quality (dropped captions, translation seams with names drifting Chen Jie / Tran Kyet / Chen Jai), yet retention-driving devices are the structure, not the polish. Story is NOT to be reused (BRIEF rule 5).
